notes.title: HOTFIX - Steam friend invite/join, Tap Out, Dodgy and online menu fixes.
notes.content:
I thought I'd get this update out before I head off to bed. (at 1am again).

[h3][b]FINALLY! Steam friend invites![/b][/h3]
You need to be in an online lobby obviously for this to work, but you can simply hit the Y button and it will bring up the steam friends list in the Steam overlay, then invite your friends from there.

I intend to eventually make this into a proper in-game user interface, so you won't even need to open the Steam overlay which will be great!

[h3][b]Online menu makes more sense[/b][/h3]
While this is really just super place-holder stuff (I will eliminate all 2D UI!), there's some changes I made based on what I saw from a Twitch stream where the players were confused at how to use a toggle/tick/check box. So NOW when you check or uncheck the "Online/LAN" box, it will show either Online, or LAN.
The same goes for the Public/private box.

I also replaced the text at the top middle of the online menu, so when you are creating a server, it says "CREATE" and when you are browsing, it says "BROWSE", because "ONLINE" wasn't really useful, you already know you're in the online menu, you don't need reminding haha.

I intend to replace these with 3D animated assets and make it way more obvious as to what is going on.

Also, I added the ability to hit the B button to go back out of the online menu rather than having to click the back button in the lower left corner.

[h3][b]Dodgy physics aren't as dodgy[/b][/h3]
I limited the velocity that the energy balls can move around at, this will prevent impossibly fast balls that are as a result of physics glitching.
I also made the ball physics independent of frame-rate, so no matter how high or low your FPS is, the balls will remain consistent in speed.
This should also help with reducing latency issues online where the server might be running at 165fps, but the client is running at 30fps, and they would see balls in 2 very different locations, resulting in death from invisible balls.
There's still going to be lag issues, but this is a good step forward.

[b]Tap Out clients no longer fly into another dimension[/b]
Something that I found was common in online games is players would be tapping away while the counter counts down, then there's a bit of lag, then the clients get yeeted upward.
This should no longer happen. This was due to a build up in force applied when the round started, and thus sent players too fast upward.
Using the same velocity limiting technique as Dodgy, the Tap Out movement can no longer surprise a certain threshold, and feels much better to play.

[h3][b]Tap Out is too easy eh?[/b][/h3]
Ok....Tap Out was NEVER easy, but for those who get the hang of it, and DO find it too easy, I added "Powermode" to Tap Out. 
At the tutorial screen, as the host, hit the Y button/Triangle and you can enable [b]POWER MODE[/b].

Powermode speeds up the acceleration rate of the camera, and also increases the tap difficulty by 60%, so you guys are all gonna get one muscly finger....or you'll get RSI....either way, this mode is for those who like a real hard challenge.

[h2][b]REMOTE PLAY DOES NOT WORK AND IS NOT SUPPORTED[/b][/h2]
I have contacted steam in regards to this, and they are trying to remedy the problem.
Due to how Metal Heads handles Input (so 8 players is easily done without messing around with XInput), Remote Play just does not work at all sadly.
I did untick the box in Steam to say that the game does NOT support remote play, but when people play the game, they get a pop-up saying to invite friends to a remote-play session, which is very misleading, and has caused some people to get real annoyed because they can't get it to work.

While it's not my fault, I still want to apologize for this inconvenience, I should have noticed it sooner and contacted Steam support sooner, but I didn't... :(
--------------------------------------

That's all folks! 

Thank you all so much!

[h1]ROCK ON![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35549911/a2929d08afed228bfd7f600644eb37840fd1cdd0.png[/img]

Today is a great day, it is a day of victory and celebration, a day where there are ....less bugs.

Okay okay, once again, I'm terrible at this speech thing, but THERE IS A BIG FREAKING BUG FIX UPDATE!

Not only that, but there's some new content to whet your appetites!

I have been working super hard to test as many annoying possible combinations that could cause bugs as I possibly can. There are still a few that remain, but I can't bear the thought that you guys are all still fighting with the big bugs, I must save you!

First up, THE NEW STUFF!

Don't get your hopes up too much, there's not going to be any more mini-games added to the demo, but there are a few new heads to choose from, along with a new mini-game mode added to Falling Apart....which is basically a new mini-game in itself!

[h2]FALLING APART SURVIVAL MODE AND EXTREME LAG FIX[/h2]
Sad that you can't play Falling Apart in solo mode? 
Well now you can, and it's brutally fun!

While it is still not finished yet, Falling Apart survival will drop tiles in patterns on the arena, and you will need to use concentration and timing to safely jump and avoid falling into the molten metal below.

This is also hilarious fun with multiple people, but I warn you, it is in it's early stages, as is incredibly difficult, especially when lag is factored into the gameplay when playing online, but I will work towards reducing/removing that at some point.

Aside from survival mode, Falling Apart got some much needed network performance increase.
I won't go into detail as to why the performance was so bad, but let's just say I durped and leave it at that.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35549911/538fb9c17512d750577861cd4bf5e10b81ab6bb3.gif[/img]

[h2]NEW METAL HEADS![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35549911/243faadf871369bc268c2ccce76c4f12a22e6fc5.jpg[/img]

[h2]BUGS SQUISHED![/h2]
Since the list is so vast and trying to get all of the fixes listed would take a while to do, I will summarize the fixes.

The focus on this update was to fix up the game breaking bugs caused from connecting and disconnecting, joining and un-joining, crashing and re-loading, and joining mini-games at various times.

There were issues where player counts would get messed up, both in the lobby, and during mini-games, and this was caused by a number of things, normally from new players joining or leaving.
Sometimes players would spawn duplicates, so sometimes there would be 2 or more of 1 character in the level, this should be fixed now.

When the server crashed, or the server host suddenly exited the game via ALT+F4 or another method, the clients would be returned to a black screen or something else, and their game would be messed up, this is no longer the case, now if players are dropped back to the main menu for whatever reason, the game will restore to the state that the game was in before joining a server.
This means no more needing to ALT+F4 out of the game to resolve these annoying issues.

There were other bugs in regards to players losing control when someone would join, or disconnect and rejoin, or drop into the game and join....it was just messy and painful, drop in-drop out is NOT fun to work on haha.

The scoreboard still has some minor issues with it, but nothing that should impact gameplay at all in any significant way. I will be working on getting some smaller hot-fixes out over time too.

The bugs aren't ALL fixed, there are still some really annoying ones that remain, but the online multiplayer connectivity is almost 100% stable.

There are obviously noticeable lag problems still with many of the mini-games, but over time I will work towards reducing this lag with things such as lag compensation and more client based synchronization techniques.

I will begin working on more mini-games again so that there are at least 30 for launch, then the board game mode, followed by character customization and other features.
I have given myself a pretty short deadline and these bugs have been holding me back significantly.

This is typically the kind of thing that big companies do with teams of people, so please bear with me while I power on ahead.

[h2]OTHER NEWS:[/h2]

[h2]I RECEIVED AN EPIC MEGA GRANT FROM EPIC GAMES!!![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35549911/d38a51e4e684d581f83e209ecee73838548c7468.png[/img]

What does this mean for Metal Heads?

It means that I have been able to finally quit my day job so that I can work on Metal Heads even more than I was and be financially stable. 
It also means I can properly afford to pay for more of Andy Gillions incredible work on Metal Heads.
I honestly don't think I can call this a solo project anymore. 
While I may be the only DEVELOPER working on the game, he is quite literally putting the METAL, into Metal Heads, and without his incredible musical talent, the game may not have such awesome music.
Thanks Andy!!!

I don't have days off, and I work anywhere from 8 - 18 hours a day, most days I work 14-16 hours however.

I am determined to make this the next best party game, and the Epic Mega Grant gave me the nudge I think I really needed to get it to that point.

Epic Games has really helped out in a big way here!

Also if you haven't yet done so, please...

 [h1]WISHLIST THE GAME[/h1]
(there is now a wishlist button in game)

It actually helps a LOT, giving it more exposure and helping me understand how many of you actually want to buy it when it eventually releases.
It also helps expand the player base, which means more people to play online with, however it's probably best to organize play sessions with your friends until I sort out some of the very important online multiplayer features like being able to kick/ban players, inviting friends from Steam directly etc.

FINALLY, I want to...
 [h1]THANK YOU ALL[/h1]

You guys help with every download, and every wishlist you make, and it fills my heart with happiness to see that so many of you are playing my game, so thank you!

notes.title: ONLINE MENU IS FIXED!
notes.content:
Hi Guys!

There have been some noticeable problems with the server browser, and I'm happy to tell you they have ALL been fixed.

Here are the problems listed below that were destroyed:

- "Find specific server" search functionality was broken.
- Setting a password on your server wasn't actually stopping people from joining.
- Buttons were not clickable after refreshing, the server list.
- Server buttons were not clickable at all, making them pointless.
- It was hard to know if clicking a button was actually doing anything. Feedback has now been added to tell the player when refreshing the server or looking for a game etc.
- Mouse cursor now controllable by gamepad, however some areas it may not work at all. (Use the actual mouse if cursor does not work).

There are still MANY problems that are present in the the mini-games. Here's a quick list of some known issues in no particular order:

- Server not being able to go back to main menu after starting server, going into a mini-game, then returning back to lobby. This will be the next thing fixed as it's fairly significant, especially if the server breaks. (PRIORITY)
- In "PIPEMARE" there are segments completely missing for clients, making it look like huge empty gaps (PRIORITY)
- When returning from a mini-game, the server can't seem to click on any mini-games with the gamepad, they need to use the mouse.
- Player count is sometimes incorrect.
- Sometimes player 1 will go dark in the lobby when a player joins the server, and the new player controls player 1.
- When a player joins a server mid way through a mini-game, weird stuff starts happening and things start breaking. (sometimes hitting the START button and
- Player scoreboard is a "bit" broken.

And many more....

One last thing to note is that the controller not working, is still an ongoing issue and I am still waiting to hear back from valve in regards to them fixing it.
In the meantime, I will be spending some time each day trying to solve the problem myself. It could be solved quickly, or it may take some time, but I will fix this damn issue that is plaguing everyone.

I apologize for these issues, but rest assured, I am working non-stop to fix all these problems to make this as smooth an experience I possibly can.

You guys have been so damn awesome to me, and I appreciate that so much. 

Thank you all for playing the Metal Heads demo and trying out the experimental online multiplayer update!
You ROCK!

notes.title: Controllers not working? Try this.
notes.content:
Hello metal heads!

It seems we have run into a bit of a hiccup!

Steam has done an update which has changed the way Steam Input is handled, and thus broken gamepad support for some users in some games (not just Metal Heads).

After troubleshooting for about 5 hours straight, I found a work-around, however this is by no means a permanent solution. I have contacted Steam support in regards to the issue, and will be looking at releasing another update soon to keep Metal Heads up to date with the latest Steam SDK.

[b]PROBLEM:[/b]
The game does not recognize any controllers, either wired or wireless. Even Xbox controllers don't work! :O
[b]SOLUTION:[/b]
1. Open Settings in Steam
2. Go to "Controller"
3. Click on "General Controller Settings"
4. Untick "Xbox configuration support"

I have tested this with both an Xbox one controller, and PS4 Dual Shock 4 controller with everything unticked except "Generic Gamepad configuration support" and it is working now on 6 different PC's where it had stopped working.

Please let me know if this works, or if you are running into any problems.

On a side note, I am working extremely hard to get Online Multiplayer support functioning. All mini-games work online, but there is a LOT of underlying work that needs to be done in order for it all to run smoothly, the spawn system in particular with drop-in/drop-out support, is no easy thing to get working unfortunately.
But I am confident I will get it done, and I will even be doing private online testing soon.

While there is no specific release date for the online update, I am aiming to have it completed within the next 2-3 weeks.

Thank you for your support, thank you for your patience.
I apologize again for the inconvenience this may have caused some of you, I don't want to let any of you down, because you guys are the life-blood to the success of Metal Heads.

Rock on!

notes.title: DEMO UPDATE!
notes.content:
[h1]THE DEMO HAS BEEN UPDATED! WOOHOO!!![/h1]

[h2]IT'S OVER 1000!!![/h2]

Hello fellow Metal Heads, I hope you are excited, because I sure as hell am!

The Metal Heads demo has reached a significant milestone, 1000 downloads in roughly 1 month! (Actually 1014 now, because I'm slow).

Ok...I know it's not much, but for me, that is pretty amazing considering the lack of marketing, and it's all thanks to you guys, you bloody amazing people! 
[b]Thank you so much, you are the best :D[/b]

As a reward for this, I promised that for every 1000 downloads the demo hits, a new mini-game will be added (until there are about 10 mini-games), and more content would be added, and more content, you shall receive!

Initially, I was going to add just one mini-game, but I decided I wanted to give you guys 2 instead because you're awesome and I want you all to experience even more fun...hell I'd let you have all of the currently playable mini-games I have made, but that would be a bit too generous, I'm not THAT nice ;)

These mini-games are.... *DRUM ROLL*

[b][u][h2]TWO NEW MINIGAMES[/h2][/u][/b]

[b][h3]Blue Ballin'[/h3][/b] (Music is different to video)
[previewyoutube=9iODEIlFil4;full][/previewyoutube]
(Formerly named Keep Rollin')
Stay atop of this big blue ball as long as possible, earning points for every second you stay alive. If you fall off, that's ok, you will respawn, but you will miss out on points.
The alternate survival mode gives players only one life in this mode, and counts upward to see how long you can stay alive. The ball gets crazier as time progresses however.

[b][h3]Dark Dangers.[/h3][/b] (Music is different to video)
[previewyoutube=q088gNRCANQ;full][/previewyoutube]
Inspired by the great PACMAN, this mini-game pits players into a maze of horror as 4 creatures seek out their prey (that's YOU btw...in case you were wondering). Earn points by collecting plectrum pickups and staying alive until the timer ends, either way, the last man standing wins.
When players are knocked out, they will respawn as a zombie, allowing them to try and catch other remaining players, so that you aren't left sitting around doing nothing.
In survival mode, the objective is to survive as long as possible.
The survival mode does not have a count down, and does not have plectrum pick-ups. 
Zombie Metal Heads will spawn in the middle of the map every so often until it's practically impossible to stay alive.

[u][b][h2]NEW MUSIC FROM ANDY GILLION OF MORS PRINCIPIUM EST[/h2][/b][/u]
Alright, so that was the longest title ever, but who cares, there's music from a dude who shreds so hard that he plays the guitar with his elbow stumps and still makes it sound awesome!
Currently, Metal Heads is using temporary music, either made by myself (you can tell what's mine because it's crap!) or purchased through the Unreal Engine Marketplace on the Epic Games Store.
While some of this music purchased is bloody awesome, I want Metal Heads to have it's own unique sound track.
It needs to be Metal, but it also needs to be fun for everybody (including people who don't like metal music) and so far, Andy has nailed it! (despite me giving him possibly the worst musical direction known to man).

Currently, you can hear Andy's music in the main menu, he has done the theme track, but his music is also in the following mini-games:
- Cognitive Collection
- Dodgy
- Pipemare
- Dark Dangers
- Blue Ballin' 

The music tracks may not quite line up correctly with the game sequence just yet, but I will be working closely with Andy on this to ensure that his music is used the best way possible.

Andy has worked enthusiastically on new tracks in the last few days, and what he can create in such a short time with little direction is nothing short of awesome!

Let's continue making Metal Heads the #1 party game to play on PC, or at the very least, a very well known party game. 
I have no doubt, with your support, your feedback, and with you all playing it and sharing it, that will happen.

YOU GUYS ROCK!

notes.title: METAL HEADS ALPHA DEMO IS OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[h1]FINALLY![/h1]

[h2][b]THE METAL HEADS ALPHA DEMO IS OUT! WOOHOO! :D[/b][/h2]

The alpha demo currently is an offline demo and contains just 6 mini-games, however I intend to add more over time to give you something new to play every now and then.

I have been working 16+ hour days for the last 3-4 weeks to make this happen. I missed my end of year deadline, but it was worth the extra wait, there are less bugs, the performance optimization I did in that time now means your computer won't explode in a firey mess, and the overall experience should be a nice and smooth one.

There are still some bugs present, mostly they are pretty minor, however it still bothers me that they exist.
If you run into any issues, please head over to the discussion forums below to report any issues and I will do my best to resolve them immediately as I don't want anybody missing out on the fun! (The more details you can provide, the better)
https://steamcommunity.com/app/1132670/discussions/1/

Things to note are:
- Xbox one and PS4 controllers have been tested both plugged in and wirelessly and they work. However Nintendo switch controllers I have only tested using a bluetooth adapter called the 8bitdo. Nintendo switch controller support on windows is still very sketchy and will only work with XInput enabled in some games, and even then, it's still not that great, so if you wish to use a switch pro controller, do it via bluetooth.
There is a guide here on how to get them working with Steam and Windows 10:
https://www.pcgamer.com/au/how-to-use-a-nintendo-switch-pro-controller-on-pc/

- If you wish to help out in any way, feel free to try and break the game and tell me in the forums the steps you took to make the problems occur.
It will only ensure that there will be less problems when the full game launches.

- It is being made by one person, I have to re-iterate, and I do have a day job, so I may not be able to get onto fixing issues immediately or responding immediately.
I will be keeping a very close eye on the forums to ensure that nobody is left with problems unattended.

I want to thank you all for your wishlists, every time I even see 1 extra wishlist, I get super excited and happy! Just the thought of any single individual person wanting to play my game just makes this all so very worth it, and I cannot thank you guys enough for that support, you're bloody awesome!

Please feel free to discuss ideas in the forums, there is a dedicated forum for this, and I encourage you to speak up and share ideas with one another, no matter how stupid or crazy they may seem, even if I don't like the ideas, that doesn't mean that they won't spark other ideas in my head, so have some fun, and lets help give this game a happy and fun community :)

[b]THANK YOU MY FELLOW METAL HEADS! YOU ROCK![/b]

notes.title: Merry Christmas!
notes.content:
[h1][b]Merry Christmas fellow Metal Heads![/b][/h1]

I hope everyone had or is having an amazing Christmas day and enjoying the time off work to spend with loved ones.

There have been a bunch of Steam sales as usual, and your wallets must be either disintegrated or crying profusely but at least it won't be in vain, you will get some fun out of it :)
I personally have been resisting the temptation to spend, because I know I won't have any time to play anything until maybe a few months after the launch of Metal Heads. There are so many great games out there to play!
If you want to play some fun little party games, I'd recommend Party Panic, Pummel Party, Gang Beasts, Ultimate Chicken Horse to name just a few.

I personally woke up at 5:20am as usual, worked on Metal Heads for a few hours, then spend a few hours with my family, unwrapping gifts and eating lots of food (Mmmm, meat platter), which was good, just sitting down and relaxing, then helped other family members move house in the pouring rain, which was tough, but I enjoy that kind of stuff, and it was nice just letting myself get completely soaked without a care in the world :)
Now today, woke up at 5:30am, and back to a 10.15 hour shift in my day job before the fun/cool stuff happens!

What is that fun/cool stuff you may ask?
Finalizing the playable demo of Metal Heads for you all to play! :D

[h3][b]The playable demo is so close to being ready[/b][/h3]
I now have Steam integration working, but there are still some nasty bugs that I really don't want you guys seeing or having to deal with, but they should be relatively easy to fix up.

I expect I will have the demo uploaded either tonight after work, or tomorrow, then it's just a matter of waiting for the demo to be verified on Steam before you guys can actually play it! :)

I am SUPER excited, but also super nervous at the same time.

I plan to update the demo over the coming weeks with new mini-games, but also any new gameplay changes, so while there may be only 5 mini-games to begin with, I intend to have a few more in the lead up to the games release, I also intend to get the board game mode working and integrated into the demo too.
It is a learning process for me, so at this stage, I am still trying to figure out how to upload the demo version, then I will need to work out how to update the demo as well, so please bear with me while I figure all of this stuff out in the coming days/weeks.

Thanks for the support once again guys, you are freakin' awesome and yet again, have a Merry Christmas/Happy Holiday!

notes.title: Playable demo news, and a message from the developer.
notes.content:
[h1]Hello my fellow Metal Heads![/h1]

I wanted to finally start communicating more with the fans and followers of Metal Heads here on Steam, and I want you all to feel like you are part of one big family, because every morning I wake up and look at the wishlist count, and it is so incredibly heart-warming to know that so many people want to play, and you guys motivate me every single day, so I want to thank you so much for the incredible support, and I cannot wait until you can all finally play my creation!

I want you guys to know a little bit about the development process, and the state of development.
I want to give you an insight into how the developer is going with it all, and I want to just be transparent as possible and talk to you in a more personal way.

[h3][b]A BIT ABOUT THE DEVELOPER[/b][/h3]
Metal Heads is developed by one person, and considering the mountainous task of creating such a project, it has been extremely difficult.
The development is made especially difficulty considering I also work a day job in a retail/sales store called JB Hi-Fi, which currently, towards the end of year, the hours have increased, and it is significantly busier, and I generally will return home and be both physically and mentally exhausted, making it very hard to sit down and work on Metal Heads all night.
Progress is still being made, but right now it is very slow compared to the lead up to PAX Australia where I worked 12-16 hour days every day up until about a week after the event,  before allowing myself to take a step back and relax so that I don't burn out.

I want Metal Heads to be the GO-TO of party games next year and potentially years to come, I want people to be excited to play it, and hopefully keep coming back to it years later, but that dream will not happen if I try to rush Metal Heads or if I burn myself out.

So I ask that you please be patient with me, as I am incredibly passionate about Metal Heads, and I cannot wait for it to bring you all together in crazy, chaotic multiplayer mini-game madness.

[h3][b]CURRENT DEVELOPMENT[/b][/h3]
Currently, I am fixing outstanding bugs every day, bugs that have been in a back-log for months, and new ones that pop up like a game of whack-a-mole. 

It is a tedious grind and some bugs I have tried to fix for 8-9 hours only to find out it wasn't a fault within my programming, but it was a bug in Unreal Engine 4, and when I have maybe 2 days free in the week to work on the game, this can be extremely demoralizing, but I persist, because it is the only way forward.

I have been working on getting online multiplayer working, and changing the spawn system so it's easier for me to work with, so that I can be more efficient in development.

I have also been spending time working on a 3D menu, which is still far from finished, but kind of cool if I do it right, and It'll be great to eventually get some feedback from you guys on that to tell me if it just flat out sucks or not haha.

[h3][b]FUNDING[/b][/h3]
While I do work my day job and it pays me well enough to continue development, my plan is to try and obtain an Epic Games mega grant to help fund the development of Metal Heads so that I can quit my day job, thus giving me more free time, significantly less stress, and enough financial stability to hopefully last me up until the release date and beyond.

Some of you may see the words "Epic Games" and "funding" and this might scare you.
The fact is that without Epic Games making the Unreal Engine, there are so many wonderful games that would not even exist, Epic Games have enabled me to work on Metal Heads and have given me and many others a great opportunity.
Does this mean I will take an exclusivity deal? No, I don't like exclusivity deals at all, but at the same time, it could make or break the development of Metal Heads, so it's something I would have to very cautiously consider and negotiate if that bridge ever needs to be crossed.

Some have asked me if I will do a Kickstarter or some other crowd-funding campaign.
The answer is no for now.
I simply don't feel comfortable having people pay me for a product I haven't even released yet.
That doesn't mean I will rule crowd-funding out entirely however.

[h3][b]A PLAYABLE DEMO![/b][/h3]
After PAX AUS, I really wanted to start working on getting a playable demo ready for you guys, I wanted a board game mode, online and offline play, character customization, and 15 mini-games for you to play, and I wanted for you to be able to play it by Christmas so that in this time where families and friends gather and have fun together, you could play Metal Heads and get a sample of the fun.
Since PAX, I got to working hard on the demo, getting features ready, fixing a plethora of bugs, running into new ones etc.

Sadly once again due to day job hours, I haven't been able to reach the target I set myself, and so if I release a demo, it would be an offline only demo with a bunch of mini-games in it, the only customization is the choice of character heads, and no board game mode.

This is disappointing to me as I really wanted you guys to have more, and I feel like I have let you all down.
So I must ask you, would you be happy playing an offline demo where you only get to play mini-games?

It is effectively what I showed off at PAX AUS, which people absolutely LOVED, and it blew me away how much attention Metal Heads got at PAX AUS and how positive the response was. 

I figure maybe what I have to offer now, is enough for you guys, so please let me know your thoughts and ask any questions in the comments, I will try to read and respond as soon as I can, so no questions are left unanswered.

Please feel free to start any discussions in the forums, and get the ball rolling for the community.
I want you all to be part of this game and this journey, and I am more than happy to get among you and be part of the conversations :)

Thank you all so much! :)
